summary: 1935 CCC lookout on Estelle Mountain, Riverside Co., CA; moved about 1958 to Hemet-Ryan Air Attack Base, where it still serves as the ground control tower; original site has a concrete slab.

facts.design: 14-by-14-foot cab on a 30-foot steel K-brace tower (FFLA-SDRC calls the cab BC-301; the register calls it C-3)
facts.status_note: The original Estelle Mountain site has no tower. The lookout has stood at Hemet-Ryan Air Attack Base since about 1958.

staffing.status: staffed by a Forest Service lookout in 1936; now the air base's ground control tower, not a fire lookout

access.note: At Hemet-Ryan Air Attack Base, a working air base. No source describes public access there or at the original preserve site.

visit.trail_note: The sources describe the tower at an air base and do not describe a public visiting route.

facts.agency: California Division of Forestry and the CCC built it (NHLR); administered today by the County of Riverside (NHLR)

events.note: Constructed on Estelle Mountain by the California Division of Forestry and the CCC.
An October 23, 1936 California Ranger item, quoted by Forest Lookouts, says a Forest Service lookout named Hutchinson hosted about twenty Scouts in the tower.
A November 1936 item from the same newsletter says the lookout spotted a fire eight miles away and sent a crew to a bonfire on that exact spot.
The Forest Service began operations at Hemet-Ryan Air Attack Base.
Moved from Estelle Mountain to Hemet-Ryan Air Attack Base. The register says about 1958, FFLA-SDRC says before 1960, and the marker and Peakbagging say 1958.
Registered on the National Historic Lookout Register on December 16, 2008 as US 752, CA 83.

corrections.why: Sources date the move to 1958 (marker, Peakbagging, and the register's about 1958) or before 1960 (FFLA-SDRC). The brief's relocation event has no year.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register says about 1958, the marker and Peakbagging say 1958, and FFLA-SDRC says before 1960. The story uses 1958 and says the sources give different years.
The register calls the cab a C-3 design; FFLA-SDRC calls it a BC-301 design. The story reports both names.
FFLA-SDRC calls it the Lake Mathews Estelle Mountain Preserve; Peakbagging calls the area an ecological reserve. The story gives both names.

notes_for_editor: The Peakbagging slab and wood-pole observations come from undated photo captions, so the story says the slab and pole are what the photos show. The 1936 items are quoted from a newsletter on the Forest Lookouts site and spell the peak Estella in one item. The public access picture for both the air base and the original preserve is undescribed. The current tower is covered by us-ca-estelle-mountain-at-hemet-ryan. No new photos added (no verified image URLs).
